key_facts: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
generated_text: An Introduction to Structured Query Language (SQL) Welcome to the world of databases! To communicate with and manage them, we use a special language. Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation. SQL commands are broadly divided into three main categories, each serving a distinct purpose: Data Definition Language (DDL) : Defines the database structure. Data Manipulation Language (DML) : Used to manage the data within that structure. Data Control Language (DCL) : Manages user access and permissions. Let's explore each of these categories in more detail. Data Definition Language (DDL) DDL commands permit the specification of data types, structures, and any data constraints. These specifications are then stored in the database. The primary DDL commands are CREATE , ALTER , and DROP . CREATE The CREATE command is used to make a new database object, such as a database, table, index, or user. ALTER The ALTER command is used to change the definition of a base table or other schema elements. This includes adding or dropping a column or constraints, or changing a column's definition. ALTER TABLE Employee ADD Job VARCHAR(15); ALTER TABLE Employee DROP COLUMN Address CASCADE; ALTER TABLE Department ALTER COLUMN Mgr_ssn SET DEFAULT ‘333445555’; ALTER TABLE Employee DROP CONSTRAINT Empsuperfk; DROP The DROP command is used to remove an entire database object, such as a table, from the schema. Data Manipulation Language (DML) DML commands are used to retrieve, store, modify, and delete data in the database. The core DML commands are SELECT , INSERT , UPDATE , and DELETE . SELECT The SELECT command is used to retrieve information from a database. It is the equivalent of the SELECT operation in relational algebra. A basic query consists of several key clauses: SELECT : Specifies which columns are to appear in the output. FROM : Specifies the table(s) to be used. WHERE : Filters rows based on a condition. GROUP BY : Forms groups of rows with the same column value. HAVING : Filters groups subject to some condition. ORDER BY : Specifies the order of the output. INSERT The INSERT command is used to add one or more tuples (rows) to a relation (table). The attribute values should be listed in the same order as the attributes were specified in the CREATE TABLE command. INSERT INTO TableName (Attribute1, Attribute2, …) VALUES (value1, value2, …); UPDATE The UPDATE command is used to modify the attribute values of one or more selected tuples in a table. UPDATE TableName SET Set-Clause WHERE Condition; DELETE The DELETE command removes tuples from a relation. If the WHERE clause is omitted, all tuples in the relation are deleted, leaving an empty table. DELETE FROM TableName WHERE Condition; Data Control Language (DCL) DCL commands are used to manage privileges and control access to the database. They are based on three central objects: users, database objects, and privileges (e.g., select, modify, reference). The main DCL commands are GRANT and REVOKE . GRANT The GRANT command is used to pass privileges on database objects to other users. GRANT <privilege list> ON <database objects> TO <user list> REVOKE The REVOKE command is used to take back (cancel) privileges on database objects from other users. REVOKE <privilege list> ON <database objects> FROM <user list> Other DCL commands include COMMIT , which saves all the work done, and ROLLBACK , which restores the database to the last committed state. Summary In this lesson, we introduced Structured Query Language (SQL) and its three fundamental components. You learned about: DDL (Data Definition Language) , with commands like CREATE , ALTER , and DROP to define the database schema. DML (Data Manipulation Language) , with commands like SELECT , INSERT , UPDATE , and DELETE to manage the data itself. DCL (Data Control Language) , with commands like GRANT and REVOKE to handle user permissions and access control.
